## FireStars

The Life and Brilliance of the Woman Who

![](images/8b4b6630e4efa156c8d92a270aae2401c3efb98bacaa46ad6b0bc7f76c88501d.jpg)

Wrapped in a blanket of sparkling space, an unformed star waits for its bright future to begin.

Cecilia kicks and cries. Until her mother sets her down so Cecilia can feel with her own tiny toes the cold and crackly snow, which isn’t soft and warm like she expected.

It’s the first time Cecilia learns things aren’t always as they seem.

![](images/9d7d922728e11adccec034882b85e62022b5fb4cef7c30623f86d1084ef0d0e2.jpg)  
In a cloud ofdust and dirt,

Cecilia spends hours watching slimy slugs glide through the garden and making friends with trees and flowers. There in the grass,

![](images/01b21ac14c64e67e601f6ec06a71068b4eda852a06b28f81c092e7a5c0a97bd9.jpg)  
there comes a sudden jolt!

Cecilia realizes all by herself why an orchid has a petal like a bee’s belly. To trick the bees, of course! They buzz over to say hello to their pretend friend, then fly off with pollen-stuffed pockets—the start of new seeds. Cecilia buzzes, too—her body humming with that lightning bolt of discovery. She wants to feel that way forever.

Yet the fields and flowers, so full of inspiration for Cecilia, are not enough for her family.

![](images/230a0f5a98e6253601d2556bf17dba8664a1404953dcd626f6109a00aa56a3be.jpg)

Soon everything shifts and separates—

Mother trades the soil and starry country skies for the sooty smokestacks of London, where Cecilia’s brother Humfry can attend a better school.

Cecilia is forced to say hello to city streets full of strangers and goodbye to the company of trees and bees.

The change is crushing—

![](images/582c77dde39fad17d90ff989e6fd777048ff2c195d8e3836e29e3d09df8d5b34.jpg)

shrinking and smashing—

and Cecilia’s sphere feels smaller and smaller still when she realizes her new school is a black hole with none of her favorite classes.

No algebra. No German. No science. Not even any friends for a shy and studious girl like her yet deep inside, something glimmers and glows.

![](images/a6a7c57332e05e4af7a5bbbc024bab375eea124a08acf10ff4bca3c9b15f94cb.jpg)

Cecilia hides in a secret place— a dusty lab meant for older students—and studies the rows of chemicals ringing the room. Here are the pieces that put the universe together.

At home she makes friends with her family’s books on plants and Newton’s laws ofmotion. In her heart, Cecilia crams every empty space with this kindling light. Science.

![](images/fe208a13f6643b584892532e3430aa112c4d13756f1083206a09968b68664ff7.jpg)  
Slowly, companions join the star-to-be.

Miss Dalglish, a science teacher, appears in Cecilia’s orbit—a new friend. She sweeps into school and blows away Cecilia’s loneliness.

Together they take garden walks and talk of leaves and flowers. At Christmas Miss Dalglish gives Cecilia her very own book on astronomy. Cecilia shines with joy.

But Miss Dalglish grows so sick she has to leave the school.

![](images/252bb5fb5d731d68e6e73238e23485943d2566fd019c3d137ef6bf4a7442516e.jpg)  
The light dims, compressed.

Loneliness creeps in again. But Miss Dalglish writes Cecilia letters telling her to stick to her path. And Cecilia does.

She becomes a stellar student and wins a scholarship to study plants at the University of Cambridge. She chases new ideas like butterflies, yearning to feel that lightning bolt of discovery again.

Yet her teachers want her to learn only the facts, to notice nothing new. Bottled up, the energy of her mind has no escape.

![](images/36862cac7dbf1c244750553a17e262e45f0605e6c99daaffde5d351c9878a7ca.jpg)  
But it doesn’t disappear. Heat builds up deep inside. Pressure growing. Never slowing until—

Cecilia hears a talk by astronomer Arthur Eddington. His work is an incandescent combination of astronomy and physics, a brand-new field to study—astrophysics! Cecilia feels the jolt, that lightning bolt again.

And her brain buzzes with the possibility of new things just waiting to be discovered. From memory, she scribbles down every word Eddington said. Then she switches her studies to physics.

In physics class, Cecilia is the only woman in a galaxy of men. The professor and other

students tease her. Cecilia shrinks, but won’t be stopped. And by graduation day she’s fully formed—

![](images/37020b77cdec340ba66a66af4ed3f278615ecc1da02b4c9d37dd950b9939280d.jpg)

A STAR!

## A SCIENTIST!

Ready to unlock the mysteries of the universe.

So when she learns Cambridge has no place for a woman astronomer, she forms another plan: a boat ticket, a trunk filled with all her belongings, and a job in America.

![](images/2c1a6ecd5c3708303ff31cf02f12d713263ec9cb569d56e0563be0fd43c029d9.jpg)

At the center of a new solar system,

Cecilia is now ringed by a circle of real friends— other women working in astronomy at Harvard. Cecilia spends hours in the Observatory studying star ingredients, wondering what stars really are. Are they made of the same stuff as Earth, as so many scientists think? Or something else entirely?

But they keep their recipe secret. As months pass, Cecilia’s hopes of solving the mystery shatter and shrink …

![](images/2d002be63b617f7fe7e6354b39915551ab765ebe205a436b519e4ee5436f8140.jpg)  
the heat grows—

the Observatory director asks her to write up her results. She’s not ready—not yet. But deep inside her something glimmers and glows, growing stronger. Something new—

and then, at last …

![](images/ce7985f3952b725fe740b0a088ef0dc1f564c7cfeb2cc0ca744c18af50450fbb.jpg)

a new light.

Cecilia blazes with that lightning bolt of understanding.

Through her careful calculations and hours of observation, the rainbows of starlight share their secrets with Cecilia.

They show that stars are mostly hydrogen and helium, not like the rocks and minerals of our spinning planet.

It’s a stellar discovery, breathtaking— but best of all, it means other questions are rising on the horizon: If this is what stars are made of, how do they form?

![](images/2d637a2029a8947f757eac59534cdc140b818b91d3263a56775f919dcb398053.jpg)

![](images/bf9ed75e0d11c3503787898107c3ca2c96289a6011aa593e954e37499c2de880.jpg)  
How do they create such enormous energy?

![](images/ffd1f773bfd642cfe48d6c55e1eafb817d7402b04d21859327cda7f51397806e.jpg)  
Whose will the next discovery be?
